sources.entry: Another Redis Desktop Manager - A faster, better and more stable redis desktop manager.[![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://directory.apache.org/sources.html)![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A cross-platform desktop GUI for browsing and managing Redis databases, advertised as faster and more stable than other Redis desktop managers and able to load massive keys without crashing.
keywords: connect to redis cluster via ssh
summary.what_it_does: Provides a graphical client for Redis that runs on Windows, macOS and Linux. It supports connecting directly, through SSH tunnels or SSH-to-cluster setups, to standalone, Cluster and Sentinel deployments, with optional SSL/TLS. Keys can be browsed in a list or tree view, searched, multi-selected and deleted, and values can be viewed in formats including binary, JSON, Protobuf, Msgpack, Java and Pickle, with decompression for Brotli, Gzip and Deflate. The README also lists stream and consumer group views, slow log, memory analysis, pub/sub, command execution with a CLI console, import/export of keys, a readonly mode, and custom viewer scripts that format values through external programs. Command-line arguments can preconfigure connections.
use_cases: Browse and edit keys in a Redis server from a desktop app
Connect to a Redis Cluster or Sentinel setup through SSH
Inspect very large Redis keys without the app freezing
Decode Protobuf, Msgpack, JSON or Pickle values stored in Redis
Run Redis commands in a built-in console
Safely look at production Redis data using readonly mode
how_to_run: Windows: download the exe from releases, or run `choco install another-redis-desktop-manager` or `winget install qishibo.AnotherRedisDesktopManager`
Linux: download the AppImage from releases, `chmod +x`, and run it; or `sudo snap install another-redis-desktop-manager`
macOS: download the dmg from releases, or run `brew install --cask another-redis-desktop-manager`
Developers: `git clone --depth=1` the repo, run `npm install`, then `npm start` and in another tab `npm run electron`
To build packages, run `npm run pack:prepare` and then the platform script such as `npm run pack:mac`, `npm run pack:win` or `npm run pack:linux`
notable: Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, with installers via chocolatey, winget, snap, brew and AppImage
Custom viewer feature lets external scripts format values, including via {HEX} placeholders for binary data
Command-line arguments can preconfigure host, SSH, cluster, sentinel, SSL and readonly connections
Supports Redis Cluster reached over SSH from internal networks, with a FAQ on finding internal node IPs
Long dated feature log covering stream, ACL, JSON and protobuf support
caveats: Some store versions (Mac App Store, Microsoft Store) are paid; the README calls them sponsorship options
On macOS, a freshly installed app may be blocked by quarantine and need a `sudo xattr` command to open
Snap on Linux may need a manual `snap connect` step to access ~/.ssh private keys
Linux dev builds may need the libfontconfig1-dev package; electron download can fail behind some networks, needing a mirror
